newsitem.title: USA: RAYTHEON DEBT OFFERING BOOSTED TO $3 BLN.
newsitem.headline: RAYTHEON DEBT OFFERING BOOSTED TO $3 BLN.

text.p: Met with a rousing reception, defense contractor Raytheon Co's multi-tranche debt offering was boosted in size to $3.0 billion as underwriters struggled to keep up with demand, dealers said.
Initially slated to come as a $2.5 billion three-part debt offering, the deal will now feature a fourth tranche with a three-year maturity, dealers said.
On Tuesday, players said the offering was issue-bid on the Street in all three tranches, raising the specter of an increase in the size of the deal.
"The deal is issue-plus bid with the 30-year tranche being the most oversubscribed of the lot," said one high-grade syndicate source.
John Huber, portfolio manager for Galliard Capital Management, said Raytheon's debt offering will be "a core holding for a lot of portfolio managers."

"It's a new name," Huber said. "Raytheon has only two other debt issues outstanding, so you're looking at a limited amount of supply and it's a higher quality industrial company that has stable operating earnings."
